title: Survival Tower
subject: Science: Evolution and Natural Selection
intro: Darwin, fitness, variation, snails on a beach and mice on dark rocks. Answer right to build your tower.

questions.q: Charles Darwin's discoveries gave rise to Darwin's theory of evolution by ______ ______.
questions.explain: Darwin's theory is evolution by natural selection: nature 'selects' who survives and reproduces.

questions.q: Evolution is the process by which different kinds of living organisms are thought to have ______ and diversified from earlier forms.
questions.explain: Evolution means living things developed and diversified (became many different kinds) from earlier forms over Earth's history.

questions.q: Natural selection is a process that favors the ______ and reproduction of organisms with traits well adapted to their environment.
questions.explain: It favors survival and reproduction. Organisms that fit their environment live longer and have more babies.

questions.q: Fitness is the ability of an organism to survive and ______.
questions.explain: In biology, fitness is not about being strong. It means surviving AND reproducing, passing genes on.

questions.q: Individuals with characteristics ______ suited to their environment are most likely to survive and reproduce.
questions.explain: The best-suited individuals are the most likely to survive and reproduce.

questions.q: The successful genes are ______ to their offspring.
questions.explain: Survivors reproduce, so their successful genes are passed on to their offspring.

questions.q: Those that are ______ adapted to their environment are less likely to survive and reproduce.
questions.explain: Poorly adapted organisms are less likely to survive, so their traits become rarer.

questions.q: Only ______ variation can be passed to the next generation.
questions.explain: Only traits in the genes (DNA) are inherited. A scar or a learned skill is not passed to babies.

questions.q: For natural selection to work on a population, there must be ______ variation.
questions.explain: If every individual were identical, nature would have nothing to choose between. Genetic variation is required.

questions.q: Asexual reproduction: offspring are...
choices: genetically identical to the parent (NO variation)
different from each other and from the parents
a mix of two parents' genes
questions.explain: Asexual reproduction uses one parent and makes copies, so there is no variation.

questions.q: Sexual reproduction: offspring...
choices: HAVE variation from each other and their parents
are exact copies of one parent
questions.explain: Sexual reproduction mixes genes from two parents, so offspring differ from their parents and even from their siblings.

questions.q: Sexual reproduction results in a ______ of the parents' genes.
questions.explain: Each baby gets a mix of genes from both parents, which is why siblings look different.

questions.q: Evolution by natural selection happens much ______ in organisms that reproduce sexually.
questions.explain: Sexual reproduction creates more genetic variation, and more variation gives natural selection more to work with, so evolution happens faster.

questions.q: A ______ is a change in DNA when it replicates (copies itself). It can make traits not found in the parents.
questions.explain: Mutations are copying changes in DNA. They are a source of brand new traits.

questions.q: Natural selection leads to changes in ______ over time, NOT individuals.
questions.explain: One snail cannot change its color. The POPULATION changes as more brown snails survive and have babies.

questions.q: Traits that help organisms survive and reproduce become more ______.
questions.explain: Helpful traits get passed on more often, so they become more common in the population.

questions.q: This process happens over many ______.
questions.explain: Natural selection is slow: it takes many generations for a trait to spread.

questions.q: Step 1 of natural selection: ______ exists in a population.
questions.explain: Step 1: variation (differences between individuals) exists. Step 2: the helpful ones survive and reproduce more. Step 3: those traits become common.

questions.q: Put the steps in order.
choices: Variation exists → helpful traits survive and reproduce more → those traits become common
Traits become common → variation exists → survival
Organisms decide to change → they change → babies change
questions.explain: Variation, then differential survival and reproduction, then the trait becomes common in the population over generations. Organisms do NOT choose to change.

questions.q: A beach of mostly brown sand has blue, green, red and brown snails. Which snails would a bird most likely see?
questions.explain: Blue, green and red stand out against brown sand. Brown snails are camouflaged.

questions.q: Which colored snail is better adapted to the brown beach?
questions.explain: Brown snails blend in, so birds miss them.

questions.q: Which snails will most likely survive long enough to reproduce, and what color will most offspring be?
questions.explain: Brown snails survive and pass on brown genes, so over generations the population becomes mostly brown.

questions.q: Mice move to an area with very dark rocks. Some mice are black, others tan. What happens?
choices: Tan mice are seen and eaten more; the next generation has more black mice
Black mice are eaten more; mice become tan
Tan mice turn black to hide
questions.explain: Tan mice stand out on dark rock, so birds eat more of them. Black mice survive, reproduce, and each generation has a higher share of black mice.

questions.q: A tan mouse on dark rocks cannot become black during its life. Why does the population still get darker?
choices: More black mice survive and pass on their genes
The tan mice learn to be black
questions.explain: Individuals don't change; the population does, because black mice have more babies.
